definition: Intelligent automation (IA), or intelligent process automation, is a software term that refers to a combination of artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic process automation (RPA).
details: Companies use intelligent automation to cut costs and streamline tasks by using artificial-intelligence-powered robotic software to mitigate repetitive tasks. As it accumulates data, the system learns in an effort to improve its efficiency. Intelligent automation applications consist of, but are not limited to, pattern analysis, data assembly, and classification. The term is similar to hyperautomation, a concept identified by research group Gartner as being one of the top technology trends of 2020.

explainer.lead: Intelligent automation combines artificial intelligence with robotic process automation so software can handle repetitive tasks and learn from accumulated data. It matters to companies as a way to cut costs and streamline work.

tiers.eli5: It is robot software that does the boring paperwork, and the smarter it gets as it sees more data, the better it does the job.
tiers.practitioner: Teams apply it to pattern analysis, data assembly and classification on top of RPA workflows; a pitfall is expecting gains before the system has accumulated enough data to learn from.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a software term for a combination of AI and robotic process automation; applications include pattern analysis, data assembly and classification, and it is related to the broader notion of hyperautomation.

explainer.example: An RPA bot reads incoming invoices, an AI layer classifies them by type, and the system improves its classification as more invoices pass through.
